cohort: The study included 29,831 patients who underwent delivery between October 2008 and October 2019.
finding: The absence of labor epidurals was associated with a significant increase in cesarean sections and vaginal operative deliveries occurring at nighttime, while the incidence of anesthesiologic complications (accidental dural punctures) was greater in nighttime deliveries.
mod_finding: The absence of labor epidurals was associated with a significant increase in the number of cesarean sections and vaginal operative deliveries occurring at nighttime.
